newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal closes higher as USDA cuts stocks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal closes higher as USDA cuts stocks.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed higher on a cut by USDA in its outlook for 1996-97 U.S. soymeal ending stocks, traders said.
USDA early Wednesday pegged 1996-97 U.S. soymeal ending stocks at 200,000 tons, down from 225,000 tons in the government's August supply/demand report.
However, soyoil ending stocks were increased which pressured the CBOT soyoil futures market.
USDA pegged 1996-97 U.S. soyoil carryout at 2.060 billion lbs, up from the August tally at 1.930 billion.
A firm undertone in beans also underpinned prices.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 35,000 contracts, down from 35,847 Tuesday, according to the CBOT. Soymeal options volume was estimated at 1,300 contracts, down from 3,190 Tuesday.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 30,000 contracts, up from 23,922 Tuesday. Soyoil options volume was estimated at 1,000 contracts, down from 2,034 Tuesday.
Soyoil futures closed 0.05 to 0.29 cent per lb lower, with September down 0.29 at 25.39. Soymeal was $0.90 per ton higher to $3.50 lower, with September up $0.90 at $273.50.
